message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) concept, the damper tuning has crowding detuning risk at midspan. To check it I used the vetted Den Hartog calculation (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3)). I found 1.81 hertz tuning with 500 kilograms total mass and 64634 newtons per metre stiffness at 13.36 percent damper damping, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose two 250 kilogram units on coil springs with viscous dampers hung below the girders, thank you Structural Dynamics Lead. My position: not ready because effective damping must be confirmed. In the same twin Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) concept, the added damping has uncertainty for comfort claims. To check it I used two-degree-of-freedom frequency response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found about 9.4 percent effective damping rising from 0.4 percent inherent damping, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose retaining the under-deck layout with maintenance access from below shown in the under-deck twin-unit layout sketch (E7). My position: not ready because crowd acceleration must be stated. In the 40 metre footbridge retrofit concept, the vertical acceleration has uncomfortable peaks under resonant walking. To check it I used the same response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found reduction from about 3.5 metres per second squared to about 0.15 metres per second squared for a single pedestrian and from 17.5 to 0.74 metres per second squared for crowd load, reaching Comfort Class (CL) CL1 to CL2 below 1.0 metre per second squared, according to Setra, 2006 and
